title: Chronicle Proxy: tenant-aware audit stream rate limiter and retention hints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview: Implement a lightweight proxy (Chronicle Proxy) that sits in front of the audit-ingest hotpath. Chronicle Proxy normalizes incoming audit events, attaches SSO/SAML and RBAC v2-derived metadata, and enforces tenant-aware backpressure and rate limiting. It will also emit cost-signals and retention-hint headers that downstream indexers and partitioners can use to make real-time storage decisions (evict hot prefixes, route to compacted partitions, or tag for short TTL).

Motivation: Current audit ingestion occasionally causes bursty write pressure and unbounded hot partitions for high-activity tenants. This contributes to write amplification, uneven shard sizing, and surprise storage costs. We need an orchestratable admission controller that:
- protects indexers during spikes while preserving high-fidelity admin action logs;
- carries per-event retention hints so downstream storage tiers can make cheap decisions without full reingestion;
- attaches SSO/SAML and RBAC v2 context for downstream compliance queries and fine-grained retention policies.

Scope (what we will deliver):
- Chronicle Proxy service (K8s) that accepts audit events over HTTP/GRPC and forwards to ingesters.
- Tenant-aware QoS policy engine (configurable per-tenant quotas, burst tokens, priority lanes for admin/RBAC events).
- Enrichment pipeline that merges IdP/SAML session attributes and RBAC-v2 admin flags into event header fields (no PII persisted in headers).
- Emission of retention_hint and cost_score headers used by indexer/partitioner.
- Metrics and tracing (per-tenant ingest-rate, denied-bytes, queue-depth, median-latency).
- Feature flags and a canary rollout plan (traffic split by tenant ID regex).

Non-goals:
- Long-term archival pipeline redesign (this ticket only emits hints; archival policy changes are separate).
- Deep transformation of event payloads beyond small enrichment and normalization.

Acceptance criteria:
- Chronicle Proxy accepts 3k RPS at p95 latency < 50ms in staging with synthetic workload and tenant-mix.
- For a simulated tenant burst, indexer ingest writes are smoothed (measured by 80% reduction in instantaneous write spikes).
- retention_hint and cost_score headers are present on forwarded requests and respected by partitioner integration test harness.
- RBAC-v2 admin events are routed to priority lane and not rate-limited in default config for admin-tier tenants.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We'll prefer eventual consistency for enrichment lookups (local LRU cache of SSO session attrs) to avoid synchronous IdP calls on the hotpath. Cache TTL tuned conservatively.
- Cost_score is a lightweight integer (0-100) derived from event size, tenant SLA tier, and recent write-rate. This avoids heavy policy eval in the indexer.
- Proxy is stateless for horizontal scaling; tenant counters use in-memory token buckets with optional Redis-backed fallback for cross-replica coordination. We will prototype with in-memory buckets + a best-effort background sync to Redis.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (staging): deploy Chronicle Proxy to staging; run ingress synthetic load; validate headers and enrichment.
- Phase 2 (canary): route 1-3 low-impact customers by tenant regex. Monitor denied-bytes, downstream errors, and cost signals.
- Phase 3 (gradual): increase traffic, enable default retention_hint upstream, and onboard indexer to respect hints.
- Rollback: config toggle to bypass proxy and direct-forward to existing ingest endpoint.

Monitoring & Metrics:
- Per-tenant: ingest_rps, p95_latency_ms, denied_bytes, queue_depth, retention_hint_distribution.
- System: proxy_restarts, upstream_5xx, enrichment_cache_hit_ratio.
- SLIs: p99 end-to-end ingestion latency change <= +10% for control tenants; write-spike reduction >= 60% for burst tenants.

Testing:
- Unit tests for token-bucket QoS and enrichment logic.
- Integration tests with indexer test harness to assert partition-routing based on retention_hint.
- Chaos test: restart proxy replica under load and assert no data loss in staging.

Security & compliance:
- Enrichment shall not persist raw SAML assertions. Only safe attributes (org_id, idp_session_id hashed, role_names) added as headers.
- Audit of admin actions preserved and marked with admin=true flag so retention policies can be stricter.
- Security review required (see security_review_required flag).

Migration considerations:
- Downstream indexers must be updated to prefer retention_hint when present; we will provide a compatibility shim for 2 release cycles.
- Backfill plan for tenants that previously had hot partitions: run offline compaction and re-partition job after proxy stabilizes.

Open questions:
- Should cost_score factor in tokenized embeddings or other payload-specific compute cost? (Triage with infra billing team.)
- Redis-backed counters vs. purely local best-effort counters: trade-offs between accuracy and latency.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/audit/chronicle-proxy-design (placeholder)
- Spike PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3487
- Indexer integration spec: https://go.redwood.ai/audit-indexer-retention-hints
